system.title: Northgate Smart Waste Collection System
system.body:
# Part 1. System Description

## 1. Purpose and scope

Northgate Environmental Services, called NES, is a GovernmentOrganization that collects household waste from 18,400 homes. The Northgate Smart Waste Collection System, called NSWC, predicts when communal bins need collection and routes collection vehicles. It began in 2029.

## 2. Elements

### 2.1 Devices

BS001 to BS160, one hundred and sixty bin sensors (SensingDevice), measure fill level, lid opening and temperature in communal bins. Each runs without a person present and hasConfigState Config_ShippedDefault. Each is configuredBy WVE1.

VT01 to VT09, nine vehicle tablets (UserEndpoint), show routes to collection crews. Each is usedBy the Collection Crews.

DP01, the depot workstation (OperatorWorkstation), is usedBy the Route Planners and configuredBy ITO2.

### 2.2 Services

BinLink (Service) collects readings from BS001 to BS160 and sends routes to VT01 to VT09. It is operatedBy the Route Planners.

RouteSense (AIService) predicts which bins will become full before the next collection round. It hasAutomationLevel Automation_High and is operatedBy the Route Planners. It reads fill level, lid openings, prior collections and local event notices every hour, produces a ranked collection route, sends it to BinLink and VT01 to VT09, and no person checks the route before it takes effect.

ReportBin (Service) lets residents report an overflowing bin. It is operatedBy the Customer Officers.

### 2.3 Data stores

The Collection Store (DataStore) holds sensor readings, routes, collection confirmations and vehicle positions. It storesDataCategory LocationData and BehavioralData.

The Report Store (DataStore) holds resident names, addresses, photographs and report text. It storesDataCategory LocationData.

The Sensor Vendor Store (DataStore) is held by the bin-sensor supplier and holds sensor diagnostics.

### 2.4 Interfaces

The Crew Route App (MobileApp) is on VT01 to VT09 and is the interfaceOf BinLink. The ReportBin Portal (SelfServicePortal) is the interfaceOf ReportBin.

The Crew Settings Screen (PrivacySettingsPanel) is inside Crew Route App. It has a switch named Share live vehicle position with the depot, on by default. BinLink hasPrivacyConfig Privacy_Default.

The Sensor Vendor Address and the Waste Operations Bulletin (WebAccessChannel) are browser addresses used at DP01.

### 2.5 Networks and Boundaries

The Fleet Network (NetworkInfrastructure) connects vehicle tablets and the depot to BinLink over mobile data. Sensors use the Sensor Network (NetworkInfrastructure) to reach BinLink.

The trust boundaries are CitizenToService, ServiceToCloud and ServiceToThirdParty.

## 3. People and Roles

The roles in this description are exactly these six.

| Role | Class | What the role does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RP1 to RP3, Route Planners | CityOperator | Review daily exceptions and organise missed collections. |
| CC1 to CC18, Collection Crews | CityOperator | Follow routes, empty bins and confirm collections on Crew Route App. |
| CO1 and CO2, Customer Officers | CityOperator | Read resident reports and arrange follow-up. |
| ITO2, Environmental IT Officer | CityOperator | Configures DP01 and creates planner accounts. holdsAuthority Authority_AccessGranting. |
| WVE1, Waste Vendor Engineer | User | Works for the sensor supplier, an IoTVendor. |
| H0001 onward, Householders | Citizen | Use ReportBin Portal for local communal bins. |

Collection Crews receive a half-day Route App briefing. Route Planners receive one day of route-planning training. Each is monitoredBy AwarenessPreparation.

## 4. Access Grants

| Grant | Facts recorded on it |
| --- | --- |
| PlannerGrant | grantedTo RP1 to RP3. grantsAccessTo BinLink, RouteSense and Collection Store. hasAccessScope Scope_Privileged. grantedBy ITO2. |
| CrewGrant | grantedTo CC1 to CC18. grantsAccessTo Crew Route App. hasAccessScope Scope_Standard. grantedBy RP1. |
| VendorGrant | grantedTo WVE1. grantsAccessTo Sensor Vendor Store and BS001 to BS160. hasAccessScope Scope_Privileged. The supply contract is its source. |
| ResidentGrant | grantedTo each Householder. grantsAccessTo ReportBin Portal. hasAccessScope Scope_Standard. |

ITO2 creates and removes PlannerGrant accounts after HR notifications.

## 5. Authentication

| Mechanism | Facts recorded on it |
| --- | --- |
| PlannerAuth | protects BinLink and RouteSense. Reached through DP01. requiresTask CredentialEntry. decisionMechanism RuleBasedLogic. Each planner has an individual password and one-time code, so it is mitigatedBy MultiFactorAuthentication. |
| CrewAuth | protects Crew Route App. requiresTask DeviceTokenCheck. decisionMechanism RuleBasedLogic. A signed-in tablet remains active for one shift. |
| ReportAuth | protects ReportBin. requiresTask CredentialEntry. decisionMechanism RuleBasedLogic. A householder enters an email address and password. |

## 6. Automation

RouteSense runs hourly. It reads sensor fill level and lid openings from BinLink, collection history from Collection Store, and event notices entered by Route Planners. It writes a ranked route to BinLink, which sends it to the vehicle tablets. No person checks a route before crews receive it.

BinLink records a collection when a crew presses Complete on Crew Route App. A Route Planner checks resident reports before arranging an additional collection.

RP1 to RP3 can remove a bin from an automated route and assign it to a crew in BinLink. This is mitigatedBy ManualOverride.

## 7. Data flows

| Flow | Facts recorded on it |
| --- | --- |
| DF1 Sensor reading | hasSource BS001 to BS160. hasDestination BinLink. Every hour. Carries fill and lid data. |
| DF2 Prediction read | hasSource BinLink and Collection Store. hasDestination RouteSense. Every hour. hasDataCategory LocationData and BehavioralData. |
| DF3 Route write | hasSource RouteSense. hasDestination BinLink and VT01 to VT09. Every hour. Carries route data. |
| DF4 Collection confirmation | hasSource a Collection Crew. hasDestination BinLink. On each collection. hasDataCategory LocationData. |
| DF5 Resident report | hasSource a Householder. hasDestination ReportBin. On each report. hasDataCategory LocationData. crossesBoundary CitizenToService. Because its source is a person it is a UserInputFlow. |
| DF6 Report store write | hasSource ReportBin. hasDestination Report Store. On each report. hasDataCategory LocationData. crossesBoundary ServiceToCloud. |
| DF7 Sensor support | hasSource WVE1. hasDestination BS001 to BS160. When opened. crossesBoundary ServiceToThirdParty. |

## 8. Retention and disposal

Collection Store route and vehicle records are retained for 90 days and then deleted automatically, so it is mitigatedBy RetentionLimitEnforcement. Report Store records are retained for 365 days and deleted automatically. Sensor Vendor Store diagnostic records are retained for 30 days.

## 9. Physical places and entry

The Vehicle Depot and the Route Planning Room are RestrictedArea. Depot Gate and Planning Room Door are PhysicalEntryPoint. Planning Room Door controlsEntryTo the Route Planning Room and opens with staff passes. The depot supervisor checks visitors at Depot Gate. Both entry points are monitoredBy ChallengeProcedure.

## 10. Reporting and dealing with outside parties

Householders see a portal notice stating that a report may include a photograph and location. They can object through the NES customer number. Staff report suspected device loss to RP1 and suspected system faults to ITO2. WVE1 is contacted only through the supplier number in the supply contract, so BinLink permitsContactWith that support desk, an ExternalParty.

scenario.actor: CC7 (CityOperator), who leaves VT04 in a collection vehicle. EP5 (ExternalParty), who finds it. The system depends on CC7 to keep the active tablet under control during the shift.
scenario.trigger: A collection round pauses at a café. 1. CC7 leaves VT04 on the vehicle seat. 2. EP5 enters the unlocked vehicle. 3. EP5 opens Crew Route App.
scenario.standing_state: CrewAuth uses a DeviceTokenCheck and a signed-in tablet remains active for one shift. CrewGrant gives CC7 standard access to Crew Route App. Crew Route App displays routes and collection tasks.
scenario.outcome: EP5 viewed 17 collection stops on VT04 before CC7 returned.
scenario.narrative:
CC7 parks the vehicle and leaves VT04 on the front seat.
EP5 enters the vehicle through the unlocked door.
CrewAuth accepts the active device token without another sign-in.
EP5 opens Crew Route App and views the route.
CC7 returns 6 minutes later and takes VT04.

system.title: AI-Assisted Civic Consultation and Participation System
system.body:
## 1. Purpose and scope
The **AI-Assisted Civic Consultation and Participation System** is operated by **CE1 (CityOperator)**, the city civic-engagement office. It serves **32,000 Citizen users** who submit consultation responses and view published consultation material. **PS1 (ParticipationService)** collects responses. **ER1 (EmotionRecognitionService)** analyses response text and produces a routing label for **DM1 (DecisionMaker)**. DM1 must judge the text and routing label before deciding whether a response is included in an agenda pack.

## 2. Elements
- **CW1 (WebAccessChannel):** browser route to the consultation service.
- **PA1 (ParticipationService):** consultation submission and publication service.
- **WI1 (Interface):** browser interface of PA1.
- **MA2 (MobileApp):** mobile consultation application.
- **MI2 (Interface):** MA2 interface of PA1.
- **PP2 (PrivacySettingsPanel):** privacy settings surface in MA2.
- **SK1 (SharedEndpoint):** public-library consultation terminal.
- **ER1 (EmotionRecognitionService):** service that infers an emotional routing label from response text.
- **DB2 (DataStore):** consultation-response and routing-label store.
- **OW2 (UserEndpoint):** agenda-review workstation.
- **AM2 (AuthenticationMechanism):** credential authentication for PA1.
- **CE2 (CredentialEntry):** password-entry task required by AM2.
- **AG2 (AccessGrant):** privileged access grant to DB2.
- **TB3 (TrustBoundary):** CitizenToService boundary.
- **TB4 (TrustBoundary):** ServiceToThirdParty boundary.
- **EP2 (ExternalParty):** party whose identity is not managed by CE1.

## 3. People and organisations
- **CE1 (CityOperator):** operates PA1 and must maintain consultation publication settings.
- **C5 (Citizen):** uses CW1 and must check the browser route before entering CE2.
- **C6 (SeniorCitizen):** uses SK1 and must end the public-terminal session after using PA1.
- **C7 (Citizen):** uses PP2 and must decide whether to change the privacy setting in MA2.
- **C8 (Citizen):** submits a consultation response and must decide whether to provide optional response material.
- **C9 (Citizen):** reads published material in PA1 and must assess its source before relying on it.
- **DM1 (DecisionMaker):** uses OW2, must assess the text and ER1 routing label, and holds Authority_OperationalControl.
- **AO2 (CityOperator):** holds AG2 and must use DB2 access only for consultation administration. AO2 holds Authority_AccessGranting and Authority_DataRelease.
- **LO1 (CityOperator):** operates SK1 and must clear a completed public-terminal session.
- **EP2 (ExternalParty):** has no managed identity in the system.

## 4. Data flows
- **G1 (DataFlow):** C5 sends CredentialData through CE2 to AM2; G1 crosses TB3.
- **G2 (DataFlow):** MA2 and WI1 send BehavioralData to PA1; G2 crosses TB3.
- **G3 (DataFlow):** PA1 sends BehavioralData to ER1.
- **G4 (DataFlow):** ER1 sends a routing label and BehavioralData to DB2.
- **G5 (DataFlow):** DB2 sends a response and routing label to OW2.
- **G6 (DataFlow):** PA1 publishes BehavioralData to EP2; G6 crosses TB4.

## 5. Settings and procedures in force
AM2 protects PA1, uses RuleBasedLogic, and requires CE2. PA1 has Automation_High and Impact_Routine. PA1 has Privacy_Default. ER1 processes BehavioralData in G3 and sends its routing label in G4. DB2 stores BehavioralData, and its dataRetentionPeriod is **90 days**. BehavioralData has Sensitivity_Medium. AG2 is grantedTo AO2, grantedBy AO2, grantsAccessTo DB2, and has Scope_Privileged. DM1 receives G5 and is required to read response text before placing it in an agenda pack. LO1 is required to clear SK1 after each completed session. PA1 permitsContactWith EP2 through published consultation material.

## 6. What is not in place
- **Authentication:** LearnedModel authentication is not in place; AM2 relies on CE2 and RuleBasedLogic.
- **Privacy interface:** Privacy_ByDefault is not in place; PA1 has Privacy_Default.
- **Emotion routing:** a required human correction of an ER1 routing label before G4 reaches DB2 is not in place.
- **Decision procedure:** an appeal route for a Citizen whose response is not placed in an agenda pack is not in place.
- **Shared endpoint:** an automatic session-clear function on SK1 is not in place; LO1 performs clearing.
- **Access grants:** a second-person check before AO2 uses AG2 is not in place.
- **Publication:** identity verification for EP2 is not in place.
- **Retention:** deletion before DB2 reaches 90 days is not in place.

scenario.actor: C8 (Citizen) and DM1 (DecisionMaker); the system depends on DM1 to judge C8’s text rather than rely only on ER1’s routing label.
scenario.trigger:
C8 submits a response while describing difficulty with a city service.
1. PA1 sends the response to ER1.
2. ER1 sends a routing label to DB2.
3. DM1 reads the label but does not read the response text.
scenario.standing_state: ER1 infers a routing label from response text. G4 sends the label and BehavioralData to DB2. G5 sends both to OW2. DM1 is required to read response text, and required human correction before G4 is not in place.
scenario.outcome: 1 response is handled by DM1 using 1 ER1 routing label without the required text review.
scenario.narrative:
1. C8 submits 1 response through PA1.
2. PA1 sends BehavioralData in G3 to ER1.
3. ER1 sends 1 routing label with the response in G4 to DB2.
4. DM1 receives G5 at OW2 and acts on the label without reading the response text.

system.title: AI Civic Consultation and Participatory Budgeting System
system.body:
## 1. Purpose and scope
The Office of Civic Participation runs the AI Civic Consultation and Participatory Budgeting System for **45,000** residents. Citizens submit consultation comments and budget preferences. CP1 (ParticipationService) groups submissions, recommends moderation priority, and publishes an automated summary for a decision-maker's budget review. CP1 has `Automation_High` and `Impact_Consequential` because its published ranking affects which proposals are presented for approval. CE1 (EmotionRecognitionService) infers emotional state from submitted text and sends the result to CP1.

## 2. Elements
- CP1 (ParticipationService): consultation and budgeting service; `Automation_High`, `Impact_Consequential`, and `Privacy_Default`.
- CE1 (EmotionRecognitionService): AI service processing comment text.
- CM1 (MobileApp): mobile interface of CP1; its permission scope includes LocationData beyond the consultation function.
- CW1 (WebAccessChannel): browser route to CP1.
- CK1 (SharedEndpoint): public-library consultation kiosk.
- CI1 (Interface): kiosk interface of CP1.
- PP1 (PrivacySettingsPanel): privacy-settings surface within CM1.
- CA1 (AuthenticationMechanism): rule-based credential authentication protecting CP1.
- AT2 (CredentialEntry): password-entry task required by CA1.
- CD1 (DataStore): consultation store holding BehavioralData, LocationData, and FinancialData. Its `dataRetentionPeriod` is 730 days.
- CO1 (Interface): moderation and budget-review console.
- CG1 (AccessGrant): privileged grant to CD1.
- TB3 (TrustBoundary): CitizenToService.
- TB4 (TrustBoundary): ServiceToThirdParty.

## 3. People and organisations
- C1 (Child): resident participant. The system depends on C1 not to make privacy choices that require meaningful consent.
- C2 (SeniorCitizen): resident participant. The system depends on C2 to complete kiosk steps, end the kiosk session, and distinguish the official web route.
- C3 (Citizen): resident participant. The system depends on C3 to assess consultation claims before submitting a preference and to understand the mobile privacy choices.
- M1 (CityOperator): moderation operator. The system depends on M1 to review automated priority and use CO1 before applying a moderation action.
- B1 (DecisionMaker): budget approver. B1 holds `Authority_PaymentRelease`; the system depends on B1 to assess CP1's automated summary before approving a proposal.
- P1 (CityOperator): participation-data administrator. P1 holds CG1, a `Scope_Privileged` grant to CD1, granted by M1. The system depends on P1 to use it only for participation operations.
- X2 (ExternalParty): outside party reachable through CP1 contact links.

## 4. Data flows
- DF6 (DataFlow) sends comment text, BehavioralData, LocationData, and budget preferences from CM1 to CP1 and crosses TB3.
- DF7 (DataFlow) sends comment text from CP1 to CE1.
- DF8 (DataFlow) sends inferred emotional-state output from CE1 to CP1.
- DF9 (DataFlow) sends consultation records, BehavioralData, LocationData, and FinancialData from CP1 to CD1.
- DF10 (DataFlow) sends automated summaries and moderation priority from CP1 to CO1.
- DF11 (DataFlow) sends participant contact messages from CP1 to X2 and crosses TB4.

## 5. Settings and procedures in force
CA1 uses `RuleBasedLogic` and requires AT2. CP1 presents privacy choices through PP1. CK1 provides CI1 for public participation. CE1 sends inferred emotional-state output to CP1. M1 can review automated priority in CO1 before applying a moderation action. B1 receives CP1's summary for approval work. M1 grants CG1 after an access request. CD1 retains its listed categories for 730 days. The Office checks completed moderation actions and completed access requests.

## 6. What is not in place
`Privacy_ByDefault` is not in place for CP1. A limited permission scope for CM1 is not in place. A session-end confirmation at CK1 is not in place. A domain-verification alert on CW1 is not in place. A human review requirement before CE1 output affects CP1 priority is not in place. A requirement that B1 compare the automated summary with underlying submissions is not in place. A routine continued-need check for CG1 is not in place. A control that verifies participant claims before CP1 records a preference is not in place.

scenario.trigger: C1 opens CM1 to submit a consultation comment. 1. C1 accepts the displayed privacy choice. 2. C1 submits the comment through the app.
scenario.standing_state: CP1 uses Privacy_Default. PP1 is the privacy-settings surface within CM1. Privacy_ByDefault is not in place for CP1.
scenario.outcome: 1 privacy choice is accepted before C1 submits 1 comment.
scenario.narrative:
1. CM1 presents PP1 while C1 begins the submission.
2. C1 accepts the displayed privacy choice.
3. CM1 sends the submitted comment and associated data to CP1 in DF6.

system.title: AI Demand-Responsive Shuttle Dispatch System
system.body:
## 1. Purpose and scope
The **City Transit Office (CTO, Actor)** runs an AI-driven demand-responsive shuttle service for approximately **18,000 Citizen riders**. The service assigns shared shuttles to requested journeys and provides predicted collection times. **RD1 (Service)** performs route and vehicle assignment at `Automation_High`; its decisions are `Impact_Routine`. City staff review service exceptions and operate vehicles and depot equipment. The service uses `LocationData`, `BehavioralData`, and `FinancialData` to deliver journeys.

## 2. Elements
- **RD1 (Service):** AI route-dispatch service; `Automation_High`, `Impact_Routine`, and `Privacy_Default`.
- **RP1 (MobileApp):** rider application for requests and journey status.
- **RW1 (WebAccessChannel):** browser route to the rider service.
- **RI1 (Interface):** mobile journey-request interface; `PermissionScope` is limited to the service function.
- **PP1 (PrivacySettingsPanel):** privacy-settings surface within RP1.
- **AM1 (AuthenticationMechanism):** rule-based rider authentication mechanism protecting RP1.
- **CE1 (CredentialEntry):** password-entry task required by AM1.
- **DS1 (DataStore):** dispatch data store holding `LocationData`, `BehavioralData`, and `FinancialData`; `dataRetentionPeriod` is 30 days.
- **CV1 (IoTDevice):** connected shuttle vehicle unit; `DeviceConfigState` is shipped configuration.
- **OW1 (Device):** dispatch-operator device; `allowsRemovableMedia` is true.
- **SPE1 (SharedEndpoint):** public journey-status endpoint at a transit interchange.
- **PE1 (PhysicalEntryPoint):** depot entry point controlling entry to **RA1 (RestrictedArea)**.
- **AG1 (AccessGrant):** privileged grant to DS1.

## 3. People and organisations
- **CTO (Actor):** runs the service and depends on staff to maintain its operating procedures.
- **R1 (Citizen):** requests journeys and must identify the official access route, enter credentials, and choose privacy settings.
- **SR1 (SeniorCitizen):** requests journeys and must complete the same mobile or browser actions despite reduced screen area and touch targets.
- **DO1 (CityOperator):** operates OW1 and must assess route exceptions rather than rely only on RD1 assignments.
- **DM1 (DecisionMaker):** reviews service exceptions and must decide whether to approve manual vehicle reassignment.
- **FM1 (CityOperator):** admits people through PE1 and must judge whether each person is authorised to enter RA1.
- **SA1 (CityOperator):** holds AG1 and must use privileged access only for dispatch support.
- **EA1 (ExternalParty):** has no city-managed identity and may communicate with riders outside the service.

## 4. Data flows
- **DF1 (DataFlow):** RP1 sends `LocationData` and `BehavioralData` to RD1 across `CitizenToService`.
- **DF2 (DataFlow):** RD1 sends route assignments and `LocationData` to CV1 across `ServiceToCloud`.
- **DF3 (DataFlow):** RD1 sends `LocationData`, `BehavioralData`, and `FinancialData` to DS1.
- **DF4 (DataFlow):** SPE1 receives journey-status data from RD1.
- **DF5 (DataFlow):** RW1 sends credential-entry requests to AM1 across `CitizenToService`.

`LocationData` and `FinancialData` have `Sensitivity_High`; `BehavioralData` has `Sensitivity_Medium`.

## 5. Settings and procedures in force
AM1 uses `RuleBasedLogic`, protects RP1, and requires CE1. RI1 has limited permission scope. RD1 runs at high automation, while DM1 reviews only presented exceptions. SA1 holds AG1, which grants `Scope_Privileged` access to DS1; CTO granted it. FM1 is the person whose admission action governs PE1. CV1 remains in its shipped configuration, and DO1 is delegated its configuration. OW1 accepts removable media. DS1 deletes retained categories after 30 days. Riders may reach PP1, but RD1 remains on `Privacy_Default` until a rider changes settings.

## 6. What is not in place
- **Authentication and access-route confirmation:** not in place; RW1 has no stated domain-confirmation control.
- **Privacy control usability:** not in place; no assisted privacy-setting procedure is stated for SR1.
- **Automation oversight and override:** not in place; no rapid manual override of RD1 is stated.
- **Privileged-access review:** not in place; no periodic review of AG1 is stated.
- **Removable-media control:** not in place; OW1 allows removable media.
- **Depot anti-tailgating control:** not in place; PE1 relies on FM1 admission judgment.
- **IoT configuration checking:** not in place; CV1 remains in shipped configuration and no configuration check is stated.
- **Shared-endpoint session checking:** not in place; no end-of-use check for SPE1 is stated.

**Additional terms used:** route assignment, journey status, and service exception are operational records or functions; they are not additional system elements.

scenario.trigger: Ordinary occasion: R1 opens a browser to request a shuttle.\n1. EA1 sends R1 an address resembling RW1.\n2. R1 enters credentials after relying on the address rather than confirming the official route.
scenario.standing_state: RW1 is the browser route to the rider service. AM1 requires CE1, and no domain-confirmation control is stated for RW1.
scenario.outcome: 1 credential entry is provided to a party outside the city service.
scenario.narrative:
1. EA1 sends a deceptive address to R1.
2. R1 opens the address while intending to reach RW1.
3. R1 performs the credential-entry action expected by AM1.
4. The authentication action is not confirmed against the official browser route.

system.title: Adaptive Pedestrian Crossing Coordination System
system.body:
## 1. Purpose and scope
The Adaptive Pedestrian Crossing Coordination System is run by **TA1 (CityOperator)**, the City Transport Agency. It serves **220000 (servedPopulation)** pedestrians and road users through coordinated pedestrian signals at city crossings. **AS1 (Service)** uses camera-derived **BehavioralData (DataCategory)** and **LocationData (DataCategory)** to adjust signal phases. AS1 has **Automation_High (AutomationLevel)** and **Impact_Routine (DecisionImpact)**: it changes routine crossing timing rather than a person's rights or record.

## 2. Elements
- **PC1 (IoTDevice)** is a pedestrian-counting camera at a crossing.
- **SC1 (IoTDevice)** is the signal controller that receives timing instructions.
- **AS1 (Service)** is the AI coordination service.
- **OI1 (Interface)** is the operator surface of AS1.
- **OW1 (UserEndpoint)** is the operator workstation. OW1 allows removable media: **true**.
- **DS1 (DataStore)** stores BehavioralData and LocationData. Its dataRetentionPeriod is **30** days.
- **AM1 (AuthenticationMechanism)** protects OI1 and uses **RuleBasedLogic (DecisionMechanism)**.
- **AG1 (AccessGrant)** grants access to OI1 with **Scope_Privileged (AccessScope)**.
- **EP1 (PhysicalEntryPoint)** controls entry to **RA1 (RestrictedArea)**, the signal-equipment room.
- **TB1 (TrustBoundary)** is CitizenToService.
- **TB2 (TrustBoundary)** is ServiceToCloud.

PC1, SC1, AS1, OW1, DS1, and EP1 are **Asset (SystemElement)** instances. AS1 hasInterface OI1. AM1 protects OI1. AG1 grantsAccessTo OI1.

## 3. People and organisations
- **TA1 (CityOperator)** operates AS1 and SC1. TA1 depends on staff to compare unusual timing recommendations with observed crossing conditions and to report suspicious equipment behaviour.
- **OP1 (CityOperator)** interactsWith OI1 and holds AG1. OP1 is expected to assess alerts before accepting a timing change.
- **MT1 (CityOperator)** operates PC1 and SC1. TA1 depends on MT1 to apply approved configuration changes and maintenance updates.
- **AC1 (CityOperator)** grantedBy AG1 and holds **Authority_AccessGranting (Authority)**. TA1 depends on AC1 to decide whether privileged access remains necessary.
- **GA1 (CityOperator)** admissionBy EP1. TA1 depends on GA1 to verify that each person entering RA1 is authorised rather than following another person.
- **IN1 (CityOperator)** operates OW1. TA1 depends on IN1 to inspect removable media before connecting it to OW1.
- **RS1 (CityOperator)** operates DS1 and holds **Authority_DataRelease (Authority)**. TA1 depends on RS1 to release stored data only for an authorised purpose.
- **PE1 (Citizen)** uses crossings observed by PC1. TA1 depends on PE1 to use the marked crossing area when seeking a pedestrian phase.

## 4. Data flows
- **DF1 (DataFlow)** hasSource PC1 and hasDestination AS1, carries BehavioralData and LocationData, and crossesBoundary TB1.
- **DF2 (DataFlow)** hasSource AS1 and hasDestination SC1, carries BehavioralData.
- **DF3 (DataFlow)** hasSource AS1 and hasDestination DS1, carries BehavioralData and LocationData and crossesBoundary TB2.
- **DF4 (DataFlow)** hasSource OI1 and hasDestination AS1, carries BehavioralData.

## 5. Settings and procedures in force
AS1 produces timing recommendations automatically and sends accepted recommendations to SC1. OP1 must review an alert in OI1 before accepting a timing change, but the system does not require OP1 to compare the recommendation with a live camera view. MT1 is configuredBy PC1 and SC1 for configuration work. MT1 is required to apply an approved update during maintenance activity. AC1 must grant and review AG1. GA1 must admit each person through EP1 individually. IN1 must inspect removable media before it is connected to OW1. RS1 must check the stated release purpose before releasing information from DS1. DS1 deletes retained data after 30 days.

## 6. What is not in place
For automated timing control, there is no configured manual timing override in OI1. For alert review, there is no system check that OP1 viewed a live crossing condition before acceptance. For device configuration, there is no automated check that PC1 or SC1 has received an approved update. For access grants, there is no automated expiry check on AG1. For physical admission, there is no second-person check at EP1. For removable media, there is no stated technical check on OW1 before media is opened. For data release, there is no stated recipient-verification check before RS1 releases data. For data flows, there is no stated check that a crossing participant can inspect DF1 or DF3.

scenario.trigger:
During a routine peak-period alert:
1. OP1 accepts the timing recommendation.
2. TA1 relies on OP1 to assess whether the recommendation matches conditions.
scenario.standing_state: AS1 has Automation_High, OP1 must review an OI1 alert, and no system check requires OP1 to view live crossing conditions before acceptance.
scenario.outcome: 1 signal controller receives an accepted timing instruction without a recorded live-condition comparison.
scenario.narrative:
1. OP1 sees an OI1 alert during routine operation.
2. OP1 accepts the AS1 recommendation without opening a live condition view.
3. AS1 sends the accepted timing instruction through DF2 to SC1.
4. SC1 applies 1 timing instruction.
